newsitem.title: USA: Tele-Comms sells part of Cablevision stake.
newsitem.headline: Tele-Comms sells part of Cablevision stake.

text.p: Tele-Communications International Inc said Monday it has signed a non-binding memorandum of understanding to sell half of its 51 percent ownership in Cablevision SA, one of Argentina's largest cable companies, to CEI CitiCorp Holdings.
Concurrent with the deal, CEI will buy a 39 percent interest from Eduardo Eurnekian, bringing its total stake in Cablevision to 64.5 percent.
Tele-Communications declined to reveal financial terms of the deals.
Both transactions require definitive agreements and final approval from both companies' boards.

Under the memorandum, Tele-Communications would manage Cablevision for five years after closing. The memorandum also states that the parties will complete negotiations on a "must carry" provision for all channels created, represented or distributed by Tele-Communications and its affiliates.

Tele-Communications said bringing in CEI would let it monetize part of its investment in Argentina while retaining both management control and enough of its original investment to be able to participate in Cablevision's growth and appreciation.
"This will strengthen our position in Argentina and will allow us to expand our Latin American distribution and programming interests," the company said.

In Buenos Aires, CEI issued a statement saying it had also signed a deal to buy 33.3 percent of sports TV channel Torneos y Competencias SA, which has a contract for live league soccer transmissions in Argentina, Chile, Paraguay and Uruguay.

CEI said the final price has yet to be determined, but it said it has already made a down payment to TyC of $11 million. CEI's receipt of the stake is dependent on TyC obtaining clearance for the deal within three months.
